newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: N.Koreans to visit Swiss, first after defection.
newsitem.headline: N.Koreans to visit Swiss, first after defection.

text.p: A North Korean delegation headed by Vice Foreign Minister Kim Chang-ryong is expected to visit Switzerland in the coming days, the first such mission abroad following the defection of a senior official earlier this month.
Swiss foreign ministry spokesman Hans-Ruedi Bortis said on Wednesday that the vice minister, in charge of European affairs, would meet his Swiss counterpart in the capital Berne on Monday.

The two will discuss cooperation and exchange views on the situation in North and South Korea, China and the Far East, he said. It is the second such trip by a high-level North Korean foreign ministry official here since March 1995.
Analysts said the east Asian communist country's desperate food situation was likely to be on the agenda.
The United Nations has appealed to the international community for $41.6 million in aid for North Korea, where floods have damaged crops and stocks have dwindled to dangerously low levels.
North Korean diplomatic sources said the delegation was not expected to visit Geneva but gave no details about their agenda.

Analysts said it would be the first such trip by a North Korean delegation since the defection of Hwang Jang-yop who sought asylum at South Korea's mission to Beijing on February 12. He was the most senior North Korean official to flee.
Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue, remains in the diplomatic mission awaiting the resumption of talks between South Korea and China to determine his fate.
